extraFacts.fact: Pressure conversion used in these answers: 1 bar = 14.5038 psi, so 100 psi is about 7 bar, 125 psi about 9 bar, 145 psi about 10 bar, 150 psi about 10 bar, 160 psi about 11 bar, 175 psi about 12 bar, 200 psi about 14 bar, 215 psi about 15 bar, 220 psi about 15 bar, 250 psi about 17 bar, 290 psi about 20 bar, 300 psi about 21 bar and 500 psi about 34 bar.
extraFacts.source: ISO 80000-4 / NIST SP 811 unit conversion (1 bar = 100 kPa = 14.5038 psi)

extraFacts.fact: FRL line order and roles: in a compressed-air line the usual order is filter, then regulator, then lubricator, with the lubricator last before the tool or cylinder. The filter protects the regulator and tools from dirt and water, the regulator sets a steady working pressure, and the lubricator adds oil mist only while air is flowing. Size units on port size and on the air flow the downstream tools need, not on line size alone.
extraFacts.source: Indus guide /blog/frl-filter-regulator-lubricator-guide; maker FRL catalogues (Parker 0700P, Norgren, SMC)

extraFacts.fact: Filter grades: a particulate filter removes solids and bulk liquid water down to its micron grade; a coalescing filter removes oil aerosol and very fine particles and needs a particulate pre-filter upstream; an activated-carbon filter removes oil vapour and odour and is placed after a coalescing filter. ISO 8573-1 is the standard that sets compressed-air purity classes for solid particles, water and oil, and a single filter stage does not by itself guarantee a class.
extraFacts.source: ISO 8573-1 (compressed air purity classes); Indus guide /blog/compressed-air-quality-iso-8573-1; maker catalogues

extraFacts.fact: Bowls: polycarbonate bowls can be attacked by some synthetic compressor oils, solvents and cleaning chemicals, and should be cleaned with mild soap and water only; metal bowls with a sight glass are used where those chemicals are present or where a plastic bowl is not permitted. Pressure and temperature ratings of plastic and metal bowl versions differ and are given per part number.
extraFacts.source: Maker catalogue bowl cautions (Parker 0700P Prep-Air II, Norgren, SMC)

extraFacts.fact: Regulators: a relieving regulator vents excess downstream pressure through the bonnet when the setting is turned down, while a non-relieving regulator holds the pressure until the load uses it. A regulator is set by turning the adjusting knob up to the working pressure on the gauge, and the inlet rating and the outlet adjustment range are separate figures. A regulator that creeps or will not hold its setting usually has dirt on the seat or a worn diaphragm.
extraFacts.source: Maker catalogues (Norgren, ARO, Parker); Indus guide /blog/frl-filter-regulator-lubricator-guide

extraFacts.fact: Lubricators: a mist (oil-fog) lubricator sends the drops it meters into the air stream and suits a single tool or cylinder close by; a micro-mist (micro-fog) lubricator returns the larger drops to the bowl and sends only fine particles, which travel further and can feed several points or a longer pipe run. Both feed oil only while air is flowing, and the lubricant should be the oil the maker recommends.
extraFacts.source: Maker catalogues (Parker 0700P, Norgren, Dixon); Indus guide /blog/frl-filter-regulator-lubricator-guide

extraFacts.fact: Harmonized System headings: 8421.39 covers filtering or purifying machinery and apparatus for gases (compressed-air filters); 8421.99 covers parts of such filters (replacement filter elements); 8481.10 covers pressure-reducing valves (air regulators); 8481.80 covers other taps, cocks and valves. Customs authorities classify combination units and lubricators individually, commonly under 8421.39, 8481.10 or 8481.80.
extraFacts.source: World Customs Organization, Harmonized System Nomenclature 2022, headings 84.21 and 84.81

extraFacts.fact: Flow ratings in cfm or scfm are quoted by the maker at a stated inlet pressure and pressure drop, so a unit sized on port size alone can drop pressure at full flow; check the flow curve or the row for the part you order.
extraFacts.source: Maker air preparation catalogues (flow curves at stated inlet pressure and pressure drop)

faqs.q: What are the Dixon Filter Elements used for?
faqs.a: The Dixon Filter Elements are replacement filter elements that restore the filtering stage of a compressed-air filter when the old element is loaded. This listing has 9 part numbers, with 5 micron and 40 micron grades listed. The listing names its use as F17 Series Filters.

faqs.q: Which part numbers are in the Dixon Filter Elements listing?
faqs.a: Examples from the listing are 5311-03 (40 Micron Filter Element), PS403 (Filter) and 5925-03 (5 Micron Filter Element). Quote the part number or the housing model and we confirm the match before supply.

faqs.q: Which element grades are available in the Dixon Filter Elements?
faqs.a: The rows show 5 micron and 40 micron grades. A finer grade traps more but drops more pressure, so choose the grade the downstream equipment needs rather than the finest available.

faqs.q: How do I match the Dixon Filter Elements to my filter housing?
faqs.a: The listing names F17 Series Filters; match the element by the housing series or model on the filter body and quote that, plus the grade you need. Elements are not interchangeable between makers or housing sizes, so do not rely on the port size alone. [Dixon FRL Combinations](/p/dixon-frl-combinations) is the related housing or unit in the same range.

faqs.q: What pressure and temperature limits apply to the Dixon Filter Elements?
faqs.a: The working pressure and temperature of the Dixon Filter Elements are set by the housing the element goes into, so quote the housing part number to get the rating. Differential pressure across the element rises as it loads, which is the signal to replace it.

faqs.q: What material and media do the Dixon Filter Elements use?
faqs.a: Media for the Dixon Filter Elements is described per part number in the size table. The rows also name the grades 5 micron and 40 micron. Coalescing elements use fine-fibre media for oil removal and particulate elements use porous media for solids, so match the type to the stage in your filter.

faqs.q: Can I change the filter grade by fitting a different Dixon Filter Elements part number?
faqs.a: Where the Dixon Filter Elements listing shows more than one grade for the same housing, you can change grade by changing the element, and the pressure drop changes with it. A coalescing element needs a particulate pre-filter upstream, because dirt shortens its life.

faqs.q: What does the Dixon Filter Elements fit and what goes with it?
faqs.a: The Dixon Filter Elements fit the housing named in each row (F17 Series Filters). Replace the bowl seal at the same service so the bowl does not leak. [Dixon FRL Combinations](/p/dixon-frl-combinations) is the related housing or unit in the same range.

faqs.q: When should I replace the Dixon Filter Elements?
faqs.a: Replace the Dixon Filter Elements when the pressure drop across the filter rises, when the differential pressure indicator shows it, or when it is visibly loaded. Depressurise the line first, and replace coalescing elements at the maker's stated interval even if the pressure drop is still low.

faqs.q: What pressure rating do the Dixon Watts FRL Regulator Diaphragms, Relieving Kits and Valve Assemblies have?

faqs.q: What is in the Dixon Watts FRL Regulator Diaphragms, Relieving Kits and Valve Assemblies?
faqs.a: The listing describes each kit by what it replaces, such as a relieving diaphragm and valve parts or the seals and gaskets of a lubricator. Seals are normally nitrile or similar elastomers, so check the oil and media compatibility if you use anything unusual in the air line.

faqs.q: When is a kit better than replacing the unit when using the Dixon Watts FRL Regulator Diaphragms, Relieving Kits and Valve Assemblies?
faqs.a: A kit is the cheaper route when the body, threads and adjusting parts are sound and only the diaphragm, seal or valve has worn. Replace the whole unit when the body is cracked or the threads are damaged.

faqs.q: How do I fit the Dixon Watts FRL Regulator Diaphragms, Relieving Kits and Valve Assemblies?
faqs.a: Depressurise the line, remove the unit or the bonnet as the model requires, replace the parts in the kit, lightly lubricate the seals with a compatible grease, and refit. Check the regulator holds its set pressure and the lubricator feeds before returning it to service.
